notes.title: Devlog 005 - Silent Forest Part 1 Release
notes.notes:
[p]Well, well, well,[/p][p]It’s Sunday again, which means… a new devlog![/p][p]This time, we’ll take a look at some of the new things added along with the Silent Forest — which also went live today. Well, part of it anyway. The first part.[/p][p]I ended up making the Silent Forest bigger than planned, so load times for this section are a little longer than I first thought. Right now, it’s around [b]37–38 seconds[/b]. Not too surprising though, since the level is packing almost [b]68,300 objects[/b].[/p][p]It’s still a fair trade-off if you ask me — once you’re in, performance is smooth, and the forest feels as massive as it looks.[/p][p]Don’t worry: lots of objects doesn’t mean lower FPS.[/p][hr][/hr][h1]What’s New?[/h1][h2]Sequence Buttons / Gate[/h2][p]As I mentioned in the last post, I’ve been working on a new mechanic: sequence buttons. They’re like regular buttons, except you need to press multiple in the correct order to open a gate. Mess up the order? They reset, and you’re back to square one.[/p][p]If you end up at the [i]easy[/i] end of the Abandoned Highway, the buttons follow shape colors in reverse. If you land on the [i]hard[/i] end… well, then you’ll be facing a bunch of same-colored buttons. Good luck![/p][p]Here's the mechanic in action on a tryout that I did to see if it worked properly when failing:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45700995/cee981d2ed1472f59ea3ac0985714f293e6b144c.gif"][/img][/p][p]And here's the mechanic in action when succeeding:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45700995/2f86a0b41436cc12f9cd3e73b6e7e6a33d569402.gif"][/img][/p][h2]Falling Trees[/h2][p]Another addition: falling trees. Get close, and down they come, cutting off your escape and forcing you forward. If there’s a path ahead, that is.[/p][p]If not? You’ll be restarting the whole section.[/p][p]Right now it’s manual (so your play time resets too), but I’m still debating whether to make it automatic like the Appearing Bushes in the Highway.[/p][p]Here's a bunch of trees falling:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45700995/98e4ec4293241c33aafb6ea09850f2e10d3bb8e0.gif"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h1]What’s Next?[/h1][p]The next couple weeks will be a little hectic — my wife’s about to give birth to our second kid (in exactly two weeks!). That means less devlog time and less progress on the game.[/p][p]I’ll still sneak in an hour here and there between diaper duty and hanging with our first kid, but expect more updates on polishing existing stuff rather than adding brand-new features.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Happy playing![/b]
– Studio Jephinca[/p]

notes.title: Early Access Release
notes.notes: [p]Hey all![/p][p]I've come to a point where I have to make a choice: continue refining things so that they work for me, or put Boll's Journey out there to get feedback from you.[/p][p]After some thought, some back and forth, some left and right, I've decided to go for the latter... In a few days.[/p][p]That's right: Boll's Journey will go into Early Access somewhere in the coming days. I've already teased about an update in the previous devlogs, and I feel confident enough where the game is now to put it out into the wild.[/p][p]I'll still be taking the coming days to put some finishing touches on the last part of the Highway Scene, a death screen and one final playthrough up until the last bit of the Highway scene.[/p][p]I've done what I can to take out bugs, lags and weirdnesses, so I'm confident that it is a solid first Early Access version.[/p][p]Spread the word, wishlist if you haven't already, and stay tuned for an August 23 or 24 release![/p][p]Kind regards,[/p][p]Studio Jephinca[/p]
